cross_sector_overview: Across sectors, fiscal and cost-containment pressure (NDIS blowouts, aged care pricing, APS overspending, construction inflation, and social housing funding expiries) is colliding with accountability and capability gaps in oversight, data, delivery and workforce (child protection, assessment tools, project governance, and ECEC/APS restructuring). It includes proposed national exams for Years 6, 10 and 12 and a national 'digital detox' with classroom screen and AI restrictions. In higher education, ATEC's next step as steward of the sector has been welcomed. Expect demand for implementation design, assessment and curriculum reform advice, evaluation of the screen and AI settings, and tertiary system-stewardship support. Outside these, ECEC supported bargaining and a childcare abuse case signal continuing workforce and safeguarding pressure.

synthesis.brief: Child protection accountability is dominating the news cycle: a damning Kumanjayi Little Baby report on NT failures, a sharp rise in SA child deaths, WA and NT ministerial accountability disputes, and a Qld minister stepping down. Patchy national data on suicide risk for children in care, together with reports of SA 'informal' removals, signals likely pressure for oversight, data and practice reform. Expect demand for independent reviews, data-linkage and performance frameworks, and Aboriginal-led child safety design, plus redress and support for Forgotten Australians.
